info.name: Flash Sale Engine
info.description:
Lock-free flash sale engine — atomic Redis Lua purchases, NestJS, BullMQ, PostgreSQL. Handles 10K+ concurrent buyers with zero overselling.

## How to use this collection
1. Import this collection and the accompanying environment (`flash-sale-engine.postman_environment.json`).
2. Select the **Flash Sale Engine - Local** environment in the top-right dropdown.
3. Run **Auth → Register** once, then **Auth → Login**. Login automatically saves the returned `access_token` into the `{{accessToken}}` environment variable — every authenticated request below reuses it via Bearer auth, so you don't need to copy/paste tokens manually.
4. Run **Products → Create Product**, then **Flash Sales → Create Flash Sale** (this auto-saves `{{productId}}` / `{{saleId}}` from the responses via a test script). Then hit **Flash Sales → Purchase from Sale**.
5. Check **Orders** and **Flash Sales → Get Sale Status** to see the async confirmation land (BullMQ worker processes the reservation in the background — poll the order or the sale status endpoint).

## Architecture notes relevant to testing
- Purchases are **lock-free**: a single Redis Lua script atomically checks stock, decrements it, and enforces the per-user limit in one round trip. There is no distributed lock, so this is safe under heavy concurrency (verified with k6 at 10K virtual users, zero oversells).
- `POST /flash-sales/:id/purchase` returns **201 immediately with `{ orderId, jobId }`** — the order starts as `pending` and a BullMQ worker confirms it asynchronously (simulates payment processing). Poll `GET /orders/:id` or `GET /flash-sales/:id/status` to watch it move to `confirmed` or `failed`.
- Send the same `X-Idempotency-Key` header on a retried purchase request to safely get the original result back instead of double-purchasing (useful for testing client retry logic / flaky networks).
- If a sale is created with `webhookUrl`, a `webhookSecret` is returned **once**, in the create response only. The app calls your webhook URL with an `X-Webhook-Signature` header (HMAC-SHA256 of the JSON body, using that secret) when an order is confirmed.
- Rate limiting on purchase: 5 requests / 10s per user, 20 requests / 10s per IP. Hammer the purchase endpoint in a Postman Runner loop to see `429` responses.

item.name: Auth
item.description: Registration and login. Login response's `access_token` is auto-captured into `{{accessToken}}` by the request's Tests script, so every other authenticated request in this collection picks it up automatically via the collection-level Bearer auth.

request.description:
Creates a new user with a bcrypt-hashed password.

**Body parameters**
| Field | Type | Rules | Required |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | max 100 chars | yes |
| `email` | string | valid email, must be unique | yes |
| `password` | string | min 8 chars | yes |

**Responses**
- `201 Created` — user created (password never returned)
- `409 Conflict` — email already in use
- `400 Bad Request` — DTO validation failed (bad email format, password too short, etc.)

Authenticates a user and returns a JWT access token (7-day expiry by default, configurable via `JWT_EXPIRES_IN`).

**Body parameters**
| Field | Type | Rules | Required |
|---|---|---|---|
| `email` | string | valid email | yes |
| `password` | string | — | yes |

**Responses**
- `200 OK` — `{ access_token: string }`. This request's Tests script auto-saves it to `{{accessToken}}`.
- `401 Unauthorized` — invalid credentials

All subsequent authenticated requests in this collection use `{{accessToken}}` via Bearer auth — no manual copy-paste needed.

item.name: Products
item.description: Product catalog. Products are what flash sales are created against — create a product first, then reference its `id` when creating a sale.

request.description:
Returns all products. Public endpoint, no auth required.

**Responses**
- `200 OK` — array of products

Fetch a single product by its UUID.

**Path parameters**
| Param | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | UUID | Product ID (auto-filled from `{{productId}}`, set by Create Product) |

**Responses**
- `200 OK` — product found
- `404 Not Found` — no product with that id

Creates a product in the catalog. No auth currently enforced on this endpoint (admin-only in a future iteration).

**Body parameters**
| Field | Type | Rules | Required |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | max 200 chars | yes |
| `originalPrice` | number | >= 0, max 2 decimal places | yes |
| `description` | string | free text | no |
| `imageUrl` | string | valid URL | no |

**Responses**
- `201 Created` — product created. This request's Tests script auto-saves the returned `id` to `{{productId}}`.

item.name: Flash Sales
item.description: Core flash-sale endpoints, including the lock-free atomic purchase flow. `Get Sale Status` and stock counts read live from Redis (not the DB) so they reflect concurrent purchases in real time.

request.description:
Returns all flash sales, each enriched with live remaining stock read from Redis. `webhookSecret` is stripped from every response — it is only ever returned once, at creation time.

**Responses**
- `200 OK` — array of sales

Fetch a single flash sale with live stock.

**Path parameters**
| Param | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | UUID | Sale ID (auto-filled from `{{saleId}}`, set by Create Flash Sale) |

**Responses**
- `200 OK` — sale found
- `404 Not Found` — no sale with that id

Lightweight live-status endpoint — reads remaining stock, sold count, and time-remaining directly from Redis with **no database hit at all**. This is the endpoint a countdown/stock-ticker UI should poll frequently, since it's cheap.

**Path parameters**
| Param | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | UUID | Sale ID |

**Responses**
- `200 OK` — `{ remainingStock, sold, totalStock, startTime, endTime, isActive, ... }`
- `404 Not Found` — no sale with that id

Creates a flash sale and initializes its stock counter in Redis (the source of truth for available inventory during the sale — the Postgres row is the durable record).

**Body parameters**
| Field | Type | Rules | Required |
|---|---|---|---|
| `productId` | UUID | must reference an existing product | yes |
| `salePrice` | number | >= 0, max 2 decimal places | yes |
| `totalStock` | integer | >= 1 | yes |
| `startTime` | ISO 8601 date string | — | yes |
| `endTime` | ISO 8601 date string | must be after `startTime` | yes |
| `maxPerUser` | integer | >= 1, per-user purchase cap enforced atomically in the same Lua script as the stock decrement | no |
| `webhookUrl` | string (URL) | if set, order-confirmed events are POSTed here | no |

**Responses**
- `201 Created` — sale created. If `webhookUrl` was provided, the response includes a **`webhookSecret` shown exactly once** — save it immediately, it's used to verify the `X-Webhook-Signature` HMAC header on incoming webhook calls and is never returned again by any other endpoint. This request's Tests script auto-saves `id` → `{{saleId}}` and `webhookSecret` → `{{webhookSecret}}` for convenience while testing.
- `400 Bad Request` — `endTime` not after `startTime`, or DTO validation failed

header.description: Optional. Send the SAME value on a retried request (e.g. after a network timeout) to safely get back the original result instead of purchasing twice. Defaults here to a fresh Postman-generated GUID each run.

request.description:
**The core endpoint of this project.** Attempts to purchase from a flash sale using a single atomic Redis Lua script — no distributed locks, safe under massive concurrency (load-tested at 10K virtual users with zero oversells).

Requires a Bearer JWT (from Login). The purchase is accepted synchronously but **confirmed asynchronously** by a BullMQ worker (simulating a payment gateway call) — the response only tells you the reservation succeeded, not that payment is final.

**Path parameters**
| Param | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | UUID | Flash sale ID |

**Headers**
| Header | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Authorization` | yes | `Bearer <access_token>` (auto-filled from `{{accessToken}}`) |
| `X-Idempotency-Key` | no | Dedup key for safe client-side retries |

**Body parameters**
| Field | Type | Rules | Required |
|---|---|---|---|
| `quantity` | integer | >= 1, default 1 | no |

**What happens step by step**
1. `PurchaseRateLimitGuard` checks Redis fixed-window counters (5 req/10s per user, 20 req/10s per IP) — rejects with 429 if exceeded, before touching inventory.
2. `JwtAuthGuard` validates the Bearer token and attaches `req.user`.
3. If an `X-Idempotency-Key` was sent and already claimed, the original stored result is returned immediately (no double purchase).
4. The atomic Lua script checks: sale is active (between `startTime`/`endTime`), stock remaining, and the user's existing purchase count against `maxPerUser` — all in one Redis round trip — then decrements stock and returns success/failure.
5. On success, an `order` row is created (`status: pending`) and a job is pushed onto the BullMQ order queue for async confirmation.

**Responses**
- `201 Created` — `{ orderId, jobId }`. Poll `GET /orders/:orderId` or `GET /flash-sales/:id/status` to watch it resolve to `confirmed`/`failed`.
- `400 Bad Request` — sale not started yet / already ended, or `maxPerUser` limit exceeded
- `409 Conflict` — sold out, or a request with this idempotency key is already being processed concurrently
- `429 Too Many Requests` — rate limit exceeded

item.name: Orders
item.description: Read-only order tracking for the authenticated user. Orders start `pending`, then a BullMQ worker moves them to `confirmed` or `failed` (with `failureReason` set) asynchronously after a purchase.

request.description:
Lists every order belonging to the authenticated user (scoped by JWT `sub`), most recent first.

**Responses**
- `200 OK` — array of orders, each with `status` (`pending` | `processing` | `confirmed` | `failed`), `jobId`, `failureReason`

Fetch a single order. Ownership is enforced — you can only fetch your own orders.

**Path parameters**
| Param | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | UUID | Order ID — copy this from the `orderId` returned by Purchase from Sale, or set `{{orderId}}` manually |

**Responses**
- `200 OK` — order found
- `404 Not Found` — no order with that id
- `403 Forbidden` — order exists but belongs to a different user

item.name: Health & Ops
item.description: Infrastructure-facing endpoints — not part of the business API surface, but useful to confirm the stack is up before running the rest of the collection.

request.description:
Trivial root route — returns a plain 'Hello World'-style string. Useful as a fast smoke test that the app process is up at all.

**Responses**
- `200 OK` — plain text greeting

NestJS Terminus health check — currently pings the PostgreSQL connection. Used by Docker healthchecks / orchestrators to decide if the container is ready to receive traffic.

**Responses**
- `200 OK` — `{ status: 'ok', info: { database: { status: 'up' } }, ... }`
- `503 Service Unavailable` — database ping failed

Prometheus exposition-format text output — request counts/latencies (labeled by route, not raw URL, to avoid cardinality explosion), purchase outcome counters, Redis pool gauges, default Node.js process metrics. Scraped by the `prometheus` service in docker-compose; visualized in the bundled Grafana dashboard.

**Responses**
- `200 OK` — `text/plain; version=0.0.4` Prometheus exposition format
